svg.text: Rory · 7-iron · 120 fps · down the line · range after work
Your hips moved toward the ball by 7% of body height between address and impact.

text.tspan: Stored on the AIcoach server until you delete it.
Unsaved clips are deleted after analysis.

svg.text: Measurement · address → impact, % of body height

text.tspan: Measured on the address and impact key frames. It is
relative to your body height, so the camera distance
does not change the number.

svg.text: Each link carries its evidence and how sure AIcoach is. The likely cause cannot be measured directly, so its leg of the route is dashed.
Route from likely cause to fault

text.tspan: Decided by the rule table: hip movement
7% is over the 4% threshold.
Measured: 7% of body height from address
to impact.
Key frames: address + impact.
Not measurable directly. Pointed to by:
lead hip turned 31° at impact vs ~45°
typical.
Between address and impact your hips moved toward the ball by 7%
of your body height. Above 4% we call that early extension, so
this one is clear. When the hips go forward, your chest has to
stand up to make room for the arms, and that is a common route
to thin and blocked shots. The likely reason is that your hips
are not turning enough: your lead hip had turned 31° at impact,
where we typically see about 45°. If the hips cannot turn out of
the way, they move toward the ball instead. So the job is not to
try harder to stay down. It is to let the hips turn while your
backside stays back. The wall drill trains exactly that, and the
90/90 hip rotation gives your hips the range to do it.
It may feel like you
stay down, but at
impact your hips have
moved toward the ball.

svg.text: See it on the impact key frame
One drill for the fault, one mobility exercise for its likely cause. Use them for the rest of the bucket.

text.tspan: Set up with your backside
touching a wall (or golf bag).
Make slow half swings, keeping
your trail glute on the wall
through impact.
Works on waypoint 2: hips move toward the ball.
Sit with both knees bent to 90°.
Turn your knees from one side to
the other, slowly, keeping your
chest tall.
Works on waypoint 1: restricted hip rotation.

svg.text: Generic guidance, not medical advice — see a physiotherapist

text.tspan: Posture angle changed 6° in the downswing. That is
between the potential threshold and the fault
threshold, so it is shown, not prescribed: no
drill.
Capped at medium confidence while it is measured from the hand
path (no club tracking).
Why does it feel like I'm staying
down when I'm not?
Your posture angle only changed 6° from
address, so your upper body stays
fairly level, and from the inside that
feels like staying down. The impact key
frame shows what did move: your hips,
7% of your body height toward the ball,
past the 4% threshold. In the wall
drill you can feel it: if your trail
glute leaves the wall before impact,
that is the move.
How fast was my clubhead?
This analysis does not measure clubhead
speed, so I can't tell you, and I won't
guess a number. I can talk about your
key frames, the 7% hip movement, the 6°
posture change and how sure the app is
of each.

svg.text: How do I know the drill is working?
